questions.question: Is it safe to ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal to ride anywhere but the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcycles: left, center, and right portions of the lane.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they appear to be:

options.text: Going faster than they really are.
Going slower than they really are.
Stopped when they are actually moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they really are.
questions.explanation: Due to their small size, motorcycles may appear to be going faster than they actually are.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is not as noticeable as a car's two brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice you, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed when riding in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What type of sign can be rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs show traffic rules that all riders must follow.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do at night since other drivers have trouble seeing motorcycles?

options.text: Stay directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights light you up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes reducing your speed, increasing your following distance, using other vehicles' headlights to see ahead, using your high beam headlight (unless you are following or meeting another vehicle), and adjusting your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Yes, alternating between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, on high beam.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to make it more likely that other drivers will see you. Use your high beam anytime you are not riding directly behind or approaching another vehicle.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before hitting it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat. Roll back the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel before you hit the object.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: Where should you ride to have the most room to handle a wind blast from a passing vehicle?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to control your motorcycle if a wind blast pushes you to either side.

questions.question: How do you brake with maximum stopping power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time for maximum stopping power. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: What should you adjust when carrying a heavy load on your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings your motorcycle manufacturer recommends for that weight.

questions.question: What should you do when making a normal stop?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping, even for normal stops. Make this a habit.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle is passing you on your left?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving toward the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Moving away from them may cause them to move back into your lane too soon. Stay centered.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week.
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections help keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
It encourages the passing driver to complete the pass as quickly as possible.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear slower than they really are. This can make it hard for other drivers to judge their distance and speed correctly.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the left side (closest to the passing driver) increases collision risk. Riding on the right side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: If you must swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, apply light pressure to the handlebar grip in the direction of your turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: How does a load in a sidecar affect stopping distance?

options.text: It has the same effect as riding without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may increase stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Extra weight in a sidecar increases the motorcycle's weight and inertia, which increases stopping distance. When carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar, start slowing and stopping earlier.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for a staggered formation. Riders on three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, not both.
Do not swerve. Only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time, not together. Braking while swerving at the same time may cause your motorcycle to fall over.
